DIS.rationale: Disney presents a moderately attractive fundamental case anchored by a durable franchise and improving operating trajectory, partially offset by below-the-line earnings volatility and macro headwinds. Pillar 1 (Fundamentals): Operating income is stable at ~$4.6B/quarter with a tight 5-quarter range ($4.44B–$5.06B), OCF is robust at $6.91B, revenue grew +6.5% YoY to $25.17B, and the balance sheet is strengthening (equity +8% to $115.31B). The Experiences segment anchors profitability at ~68-72% of operating income. DTC streaming has inflected to $1.3B operating income in FY2025 from $143M prior year. However, EPS declined -29.8% YoY ($1.27 vs $1.81) due to below-the-line items, creating earnings visibility uncertainty. Management guides ~12% adjusted EPS growth for FY2026. Pillar 2 (Valuation): PE of 14.88x is near the bottom of its 12.5x–23.8x trailing range and well below the 21.33x level of one year ago — a ~30% compression. Earnings yield of 6.7% exceeds the 10Y Treasury at 4.57% by 213bps. P/B of 1.592x is near the floor of its 1.5x–2.1x range. The market is paying materially less for Disney's operating earnings than a year ago, which appears to overstate the fundamental deterioration given stable operating margins. Pillar 3 (Near-term catalyst): Q2 FY2026 earnings beat ($1.57 vs $1.49 consensus) reported ~May 6, 2026, with Citi raising its PT to $145. The new CEO's super-app strategy and $60B parks capex program provide a forward growth narrative. However, the FCC ABC license review (ordered April 28, 2026) introduces regulatory overhang, and oil at $100.20/barrel (+51% since Feb) is a direct cost headwind for parks. These offsetting near-term factors limit the catalyst boost. Net: a solid franchise at a meaningful discount to its own history, with improving DTC economics and parks investment, but tempered by below-the-line earnings noise, rising macro headwinds, and regulatory uncertainty. Score of +0.3 reflects mild-to-moderate attractiveness.

10Y Treasury yield at 4.57% (+13.4% since late Feb) and Baa spread at 6.16% represent rising cost-of-capital headwinds
